benchmark.instrument: 444-slice pinned typesweep (decbench 625e892 via final-c/pindb.py), finalsweep, --workers 12; ALL arms built from this tree (.scratch/arm-base = origin/main, arm-new = the table alone, arm-fix = what ships: the table plus the placeholder strip)
benchmark.control: the base arm reproduces round F exactly: 1,522 perfect, mean .3553, aggregate 3818.77

bool.note: the placeholder strip's whole cost: -10, the only class that moves against the table-alone arm

benchmark.worse_rows_read: All four are the placeholder strip, not the table: against the table-alone arm the table has 0 worse rows, and the strip alone is 0 improved / 4 worse / aggregate -0.31. Every one is the same class -- a GT `_Bool` one-byte stack local that spelled `bool` and now spells `char`, in two distinct functions (ls/dir/vdir are one program). Both functions have an alloca-shaped frame whose stack pointer is itself a variable, which is the shape that kept the placeholder in the first place. It is core type inference, not `boolbyte`: `--option boolbyte off` changes neither arm's rendering of those slots.

placeholder_strip.what: Heritage::clearStackPlaceholders was an unported stub (only the flag was cleared), so the stack-pointer placeholder ActionFuncLink appends to every CALL was never removed from a call whose callee carries a DECLARED prototype -- such a call's input list is locked, so no later pass rewrites it. It rendered as one argument past the declared arity, reading the slot the `call` pushed its return address into.
placeholder_strip.pre_existing: On origin/main, ginstall alone renders 13 such calls (free, strlen, strcmp, stat, fstatat ...); the widened table made the class visible on 24 more sites because it declares 333 more names. Both arms are fixed.
placeholder_strip.no_option: A strict bug fix: the emitted call contradicted the prototype the same output declares, and reading the return-address slot has no reading under which it is right.
placeholder_strip.gates: make test 675/675 PARITY OK and make test-stages PARITY OK with ZERO moved assertions; the only new keys are the three KUNA-CALLPLACEHOLDER ones.
